transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

Well, I came in because I just can't seem to stop worrying about... everything, really. My mind is constantly jumping around. Like, one minute I'm stressing about whether our lab's new partnership is going to cut my position, and the next I'm terrified that my data from last week is all wrong. Then it spirals into worrying about my bills piling up, or that my family thinks I'm falling behind, or... or whether I've already ruined my chances at getting into grad school. It's just non-stop.
How long have you been experiencing this ongoing, hard-to-control worry?

It's been... I'd say about seven months. Yeah, right around seven months. It started when the lab had this big funding shift. We got a new commercial partnership, and it basically changed how everything was being run there. That's when all this really kicked off.
When you are not thinking about the lab partnership, do you still find yourself unable to control worry about other areas of your life?

Yeah, absolutely. It doesn't really matter if I'm thinking about the partnership or not. I'll try to just... tell myself to focus on one specific task, you know? Like, just finish this one report, or just check this one assay. But it doesn't work. One worry just kind of... sets off another one. And before I know it, I'm just sitting there staring at my computer screen, and my head is just running through every single possible way things could go wrong in my life. It's really hard to stop it once it starts.
On days when nothing related to the lab partnership is happening, does the same level of worry still occur?

Yeah, it... it really does. Even on weekends or days when I'm not at the lab at all, the worry is just as intense. It's like my brain just finds something else to latch onto instead, like my bills or the grad school stuff I mentioned earlier. The anxiety doesn't ever really take a day off, even if I do.
Before the lab’s funding shift, were you already experiencing this same kind of excessive worry across multiple areas of your life?

No, not really. I mean, I had normal stress before that, just from working in the lab and dealing with school stuff. But it was never like this. It never... took over everything. Before the funding shift, if I had a day off, I could actually just relax and not think about things. This constant, everyday worrying really just started about seven months ago.
Do you have difficulty concentrating because of the worry?

Yeah, I really do. It's like... I'll be trying to read a paper or run an experiment, and my mind just completely drifts off to whatever I'm worried about that day. I end up having to re-read the same paragraph three or four times because I just can't focus on the words. It makes getting anything done take twice as long.
Have you been having trouble sleeping because of your worry?

No, my sleep hasn't really been affected. I mean, I might take a little longer to fall asleep sometimes because my mind is racing, but once I'm out, I usually sleep through the night. I'm just exhausted by the end of the day from dealing with all the stress, so I haven't really had trouble with sleeping itself.
Do you often feel restless or keyed up, as if it is difficult to relax or sit still?

Yeah, I do. Especially at work. I just feel... wound up, I guess. Like I can't really settle into my chair. I end up tapping my foot constantly or checking my messages when I don't need to. Sometimes I'll just get up and walk back to the instrument room for no real reason, just because I can't sit still. And I've noticed I'm kind of jumpy, too—like, just normal lab noises will startle me.
